entry.title: Could a simple tampon help detect ovarian cancer earlier? 🧬

media:group.media:title: Could a simple tampon help detect ovarian cancer earlier? 🧬
media:group.media:description:
In Ep 10 of Ask the Expert, Dr Jemma Longley explains how vaginal fluid-derived biomarkers and tiny molecules called microRNAs could help identify the early signs of ovarian cancer.
MicroRNAs help regulate how our cells work, and changes in these tiny molecules could provide important biological clues about what's happening inside the body.
The demonstrations shown are for illustrative purposes only and are not intended to represent practical laboratory procedures.

entry.title: EPISODE 11 Path to Uni: The Awarding Gap Project | University of Southampton

media:group.media:title: EPISODE 11 Path to Uni: The Awarding Gap Project | University of Southampton
media:group.media:description:
University should be about more than getting a degree. It’s about finding your place, feeling supported, being able to be yourself and knowing your voice can make a difference.
At Southampton, the Awarding Gap Project brings students and staff together to help create a more inclusive university experience for Black and marginalised minority ethnic students. With student voices driving the work, the project looks at community, culture and curriculum, and how each can help tackle inequalities in student outcomes.
In this episode of Southampton Sessions: Path to Uni, project members Amma, Runoh, Tise and Jonathan join Chido, Student Inclusion Manager, to talk openly about belonging, representation and what it takes to create meaningful change.
They share how the project started, what they’ve learned along the way and how students can help shape the university experience they want to see. They also explore what getting involved can offer personally, from new connections and skills to paid work experience.

entry.title: Mapping historic documents into maps using AI

media:group.media:title: Mapping historic documents into maps using AI
media:group.media:description:
Historians have created a first-of-its-kind online interactive map, using data from hundreds of thousands of pages of centuries-old port records to chart Britain’s growth into a dominant global trading nation.
The University of Southampton project used artificial intelligence to transform information from delicate handwritten ‘port books’ into an enormous database of Britain’s merchant shipping past. It charts the country’s growth into an Empire during the late-16th to mid-18th century – from the reign of Elizabeth I to George III.

entry.title: Making your application stand out | University of Southampton

media:group.media:title: Making your application stand out | University of Southampton
media:group.media:description:
Your application doesn’t need the most impressive story. It needs your story.
How do you make your university application stand out? It’s not about having the longest list of achievements. It’s about choosing the experiences that matter and showing what you’ve learnt from them.
In this University of Southampton Quick 5, we’ll help you approach your UCAS personal statement with purpose, bringing together your interests, experiences and motivation for studying your chosen subject.
We’ll explore: 1️⃣ Why universities ask for a personal statement 2️⃣ How to structure your answers clearly 3️⃣ What to include in each section 4️⃣ How to reflect on your experiences and make them count 5️⃣ How to bring everything together in your own voice
There’s no single formula for a “perfect” personal statement. What matters is showing admissions teams what drives you, what you’ve learnt and why you’re ready to take your subject further.
Ready to turn your experiences into an application that stands out?

entry.title: What do the public want from the railways?

media:group.media:title: What do the public want from the railways?
media:group.media:description:
RailBreak is an interactive installation featuring a collaborative tabletop game and working model railway. Players of the game make decisions about improving Britain's railways and see their choices play out in real-time.
It's part of a sandpit funded interdisciplinary project with a team from across the University of Southampton and Winchester School of Art, in games design, electronics, music and sociology.
The team hosted this showcase event at the Bitterne Station Community Hub in February with help from local nonprofit Bunker178. Parts of the model railway were supplied by a model train shop in Shirley called Ronlines. It was a very friendly atmosphere as members of the public engaged with the game. They shared their experiences of the railway and discussed what they want from the railway as we head into a deprivatised future.
